- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.4) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to capture mean reversion.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8) and prices show no clear trend, model overfits noise; use 5-day SMA or ignore sentiment if >2 consecutive days of low sentiment.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates in early periods (first 5–7 days) after a spike; add 0.5–1.5% bias to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or rising.  
- If sentiment is consistently 0.8+ over 3+ days, model overestimates; apply 1–2% downward correction to avoid overbought bias.  
- If sentiment drops sharply (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.2) and price falls, model often fails to catch the drop; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to avoid underestimating downside.
